newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on LME heavy losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on LME heavy losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply down in active trading on Friday on heavy overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at an intra-day low of 23,480 yuan ($2,830) per tonne, losing 420 yuan. It opened at a high of 23,700.
April fell 130 to 23,330, May 230 to 23,350, June 390 to 23,390, August 470 to 23,500 and September 400 to 23,510.
Combined volume rose sharply to 93,850 tonnes from 22,690.
Traders said the copper contracts opened lower and fell further for most of the session.
They said LME losses discouraged long-term investors in Shangahi from building positions.

"Large amounts of stop loss orders emerged today and few investors dared to buy," one trader said. "With no domestic market-moving news in sight, the LME price movements will have a decisive impact on the Shanghai market in the next few days."
Traders said Friday's fall hurt market sentiment and the short-term outlook was not optimistic.
"It will need some time for investors to recover their confidence unless prices on the LME surge," said a second trader.
Metal analysts warn that it would be risky to bet on price rises in the short term but also warned that it woulkd be premature for long-term short sellers to build heavy positions immediately.
"A better strategy is to wait and seen in the short term," a copper analyst said.
Aluminium futures ended sharply down following copper's trend, traders said.
April fell 250 yuan to 15,750, May 330 to 15,950, June 350 to 16,150 and July 300 to 16,300.
Combined volume rose to 3,410 tonnes from 2,370.
